s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of neurological symptoms with transient loss of consciousness, seizures, and visual disturbances in a young woman with recent menstrual irregularities and elevated tumor markers
salient_findings: Transient loss of consciousness lasting a few minutes
Cystic lesion in third ventricle with upstream ventriculomegaly on head CT
key_facts: 19-year-old woman presented to the emergency department
Transient loss of consciousness lasting a few minutes
Ongoing metrorrhagia three weeks after regular menses
Globular abdomen without tenderness or masses on palpation

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of neurological symptoms with transient loss of consciousness, seizures, and visual disturbances in a young woman with recent menstrual irregularities and elevated tumor markers
salient_findings: Transient loss of consciousness lasting a few minutes
Cystic lesion in third ventricle with upstream ventriculomegaly on head CT
key_facts: 19-year-old woman presented to the emergency department
Transient loss of consciousness lasting a few minutes
Ongoing metrorrhagia three weeks after regular menses
Globular abdomen without tenderness or masses on palpation

shortlist.label: Choriocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated β-HCG levels and recent menstrual irregularities

shortlist.label: Germinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated β-HCG levels and presence of hypothalamic hamartoma

shortlist.label: Hypothalamic hamartoma
shortlist.why_kept: Directly identified in brain MRI and associated with seizures

shortlist.label: Arachnoid cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Identified in brain MRI and potential cause of neurological symptoms

shortlist.label: Pituitary adenoma
shortlist.why_kept: Potential cause of elevated tumor markers and hormonal imbalance

raw.rationale: Elevated β-HCG levels, which are significantly high and then decreased, along with symptoms such as nausea, vomiting, and metrorrhagia, are indicative of a pregnancy-related condition. The presence of elevated α-fetoprotein and CA-125 levels also supports this diagnosis, as these can be associated with certain types of gestational trophoblastic disease, including choriocarcinoma.

rejected.label: Germinoma
rejected.why: While germinomas can cause elevated β-HCG levels, the clinical presentation and significant elevation of β-HCG followed by a decrease is more suggestive of choriocarcinoma.

rejected.label: Hypothalamic hamartoma
rejected.why: Hypothalamic hamartomas can cause seizures and other neurological symptoms but do not typically cause the significant elevation in β-HCG levels seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Arachnoid cyst
rejected.why: Arachnoid cysts are benign lesions that do not typically cause systemic symptoms such as nausea, vomiting, or elevated tumor markers like β-HCG.

rejected.label: Pituitary adenoma
rejected.why: Pituitary adenomas can cause a variety of symptoms depending on their type, but the significant elevation in β-HCG and the clinical presentation are not typical for a pituitary adenoma.
